items.title: We’ll likely have 1,000X more tokens flowing through cyber agents soon than we do today
items.text: We’ll likely have 1,000X more tokens flowing through cyber agents soon than we do today. As the surface area of cyber risk increases, at some point soon it will be nearly impossible to keep up with the volume of new risks (we’re essentially already there). Large companies barely had the resources to pull this off before, but the vast majority of companies don’t. There’s a never ending set of libraries to keep up with, tools to leverage, and sprawling infrastructure and code to secure. We’ll have agent swarms that can fan out, leverage any security tool, test various perpetuations of attacks, read through logs, process enterprise data for risk level, and more. items.text: I oddly love the models' engineering vernacular: gate, evidence, culprit, durable, provenance, contract… A lot of these stem from most engineering being debugging and understanding existing systems, where you take on the detective / auditor roles. You do forensics. I wonder what the *minimum viable English* in fact is to be productive. ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English contains ~900 approved words. I suspect we need far fewer.

items.title: Of all the learning apps that my 4-year-old and I have tried, @once_reading is the only one tha...
items.text: Of all the learning apps that my 4-year-old and I have tried, @once_reading is the only one that we’ve managed to persist in following for months. It works because: 1. It builds a habit where you need to learn with your kid daily 2. It has lightweight gamification like taking a silly photo with your kid after every lesson 3. After 30 lessons, Once will send you books for your kid to read by themselves, giving them a big feeling of accomplishment My kid loves reading now and will even choose her Once books over YouTube and the phone (sometimes at least) which is the highest compliment 😅 This is not sponsored or anything I just love the product. Try out Once here: https://t.co/RbDiwACYbI
